name: Feelory
summary: Journal with feeling tags and intensity, make quick check-ins, and explore 128 emotions. Personal by design, local by default.
headline: Find words for what you feel.
compatibility: Made for iPhone and iPad, with support for compatible Macs through Designed for iPad.

hero.alt: Feelory journal screen with a written entry and its selected feeling tags.

secondaryHero.name: tablet-reflection
secondaryHero.alt: Feelory on iPad showing a journal reflection and selected feeling tags.

features.title: Notice patterns, not scores.
paragraphs: Insights help you notice which emotion families appear in your reflections, how pleasantness varies, and when feelings tend to show up.
These patterns are invitations to reflect, not diagnoses or judgments.

media.name: phone-insights
media.alt: Feelory Insights charts showing feeling patterns across synthetic reflections.

features.caption: Illustrative patterns from synthetic reflections, not an assessment.

features.title: Practice a little at a time.
paragraphs: Flashcards and quizzes help you get to know nearby feelings. There is no need to get your own emotions "right".

Quick check-ins can be just a feeling and an optional note. The default is one gentle reminder each evening at 8 PM local time; choose reminder days and times in Settings, up to eight a day. Widgets, Shortcuts, and a Control Center control help you pause when the moment is right.

media.name: phone-practice
media.alt: Feelory practice screen with a flashcard about an emotion.

features.caption: Learn a little at a time with flashcards and quizzes.

features.title: Find a feeling by name or family.
paragraphs: Explore 128 emotions across eight families. Read definitions, everyday examples, and body sensations, then compare nearby feelings.
Search by a word or sensation when you know what you notice but not what to call it.

media.name: phone-explore
media.alt: Feelory Explore screen listing emotions and family filters.

features.caption: Explore emotions by name, family, or body sensation.

features.title: Start with the shape of a feeling.
paragraphs: The emotion wheel helps you explore feelings when you have a sense of the emotion but not its name. Matching feelings appear beneath the wheel.

media.name: phone-wheel
media.alt: Feelory emotion wheel with matching feelings listed beneath it.

features.caption: The wheel connects a broad emotion to matching feelings.

features.title: Get to know each emotion.
paragraphs: Open an emotion to explore its meaning and related details. Keep journaling with multiple feeling tags and add intensity when it helps; your writing saves as a draft while you go.
Optional on-device AI suggestions are included when Apple Intelligence is available on a supported device. They run entirely on your device with no remote fallback. Feelory works without them.

features.caption: Explore an emotion in context; screen examples use synthetic content.
